articles.title: Amid accident deaths, Keralam Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala warns of crackdown on intoxicated driving
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Minister visits family of Cheranalloor crash victim Jayabalakrishnan, says accidents caused by intoxicated drivers, claiming the lives of innocent people, have become widespread in the State
Keralam Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala has warned of a strict police crackdown on driving under the influence of alcohol and drugs.

He was speaking to the media on Saturday (October 31, 2026) after visiting the family of Jayabalakrishnan , who was mowed down by a speeding car allegedly driven by the minor son of an additional judge, at Cheranalloor near Kochi.

Mr. Chennithala said that accidents caused by intoxicated drivers, claiming the lives of innocent people, have become widespread in the State. This cannot be allowed, he said, urging people to cooperate and not complain later.

Asked about making the law more stringent in the wake of the Cheranalloor crash, the Minister said the government would consider it seriously. He added that the State government was committed to ensuring justice for the family of the victim.

“The government will remain firmly with the family and ensure that justice is delivered. Law and justice are the same for all, whether it is a judge or a common man. The police have already moved the court to cancel the bail of the minor accused. The family is satisfied with the action taken by the government,” said Mr. Chennithala, who, however, downplayed the error in the appeal filed for suspension of bail.

The Ernakulam Additional District and Sessions Court, which tries cases involving atrocities against women and children, criticised the appeal application for revealing details identifying the minor. The court is set to hear the appeal later on Saturday.

Jayabalakrishnan’s daughter, Bhadra Keerthy, expressed confidence in the assurances given by both the Chief Minister and the Home Minister. Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan had visited the family on Friday (October 30, 2026).
Mr. Chennithala was accompanied by Hibi Eden, MP, T. J. Vinod, MLA, and District Police Chief (Kochi City) R. Nishanthini.

Mr. Chennithala said that accidents caused by intoxicated drivers, claiming the lives of innocent people, have become widespread in the State. This cannot be allowed, he said, urging people to cooperate and not complain later.

Asked about making the law more stringent in the wake of the Cheranalloor crash, the Minister said the government would consider it seriously. He added that the State government was committed to ensuring justice for the family of the victim.

“The government will remain firmly with the family and ensure that justice is delivered. Law and justice are the same for all, whether it is a judge or a common man. The police have already moved the court to cancel the bail of the minor accused. The family is satisfied with the action taken by the government,” said Mr. Chennithala, who, however, downplayed the error in the appeal filed for suspension of bail.

The Ernakulam Additional District and Sessions Court, which tries cases involving atrocities against women and children, criticised the appeal application for revealing details identifying the minor. The court is set to hear the appeal later on Saturday.

Jayabalakrishnan’s daughter, Bhadra Keerthy, expressed confidence in the assurances given by both the Chief Minister and the Home Minister. Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan had visited the family on Friday (October 30, 2026).

Mr. Chennithala was accompanied by Hibi Eden, MP, T. J. Vinod, MLA, and District Police Chief (Kochi City) R. Nishanthini.

articles.title: West Bengal steps up efforts to bring back tigress that strayed into Assam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: West Bengal Forest Minister Manoj Oraon is all set to visit the tigress in Assam and finalise the plan to tranquilise it and bring back to Bengal’s territory
The West Bengal government is planning to bring back a tigress that was released in the Buxa Tiger Reserve and later strayed into Assam.

The three-year-old tigress, BTR-TF-1 (T-138), was released in Buxa on October 2 from Bihar’s Valmiki Tiger Reserve as part of the State’s first tiger relocation project. However, the tigress crossed into Assam on Sunday (October 25, 2026) in search of a suitable habitat.
West Bengal Forest Minister Manoj Oraon said that he and officers of the department will visit Assam on Saturday (October 31, 2026) to inspect the tigress’s movement and health condition.

fullParagraphs: Tehran has restricted maritime traffic through the strait since the West Asia war erupted on February 28 with U.S.-Israeli strikes on the Islamic republic

Tehran has restricted maritime traffic through the strait since the West Asia war erupted on February 28 with U.S.-Israeli strikes on the Islamic republic.
The narrow waterway, which normally carries about a fifth of global oil, has become a focal point of the conflict, with ships regularly coming under Iranian fire.

Muscat's navy "carried out an evacuation operation for 25 crew members of the merchant ship RITI, flying the Panamanian flag, after it was targeted, which led to a fire breaking out on board," Oman's Maritime Security Centre said in a statement.
The crew members were provided with medical care, the Omani statement said, without giving details.

U.S. forces remain "present to ensure that all primary transit routes in the Strait of Hormuz remain free and clear," he added.

Mr. Cooper said he visited some of the more than 50,000 U.S. service members in the region, repeating earlier statements that Washington has helped Gulf countries export more than 1.5 billion barrels of crude via the strait since summer.

British maritime security agency UKMTO said that a ship 40 nautical miles (74 kilometres) south of Lavan Island in Iran was struck on Friday (October 30) by an unknown projectile, which caused a fire onboard.

articles.title: Fears of violence as France braces for Halloween protests
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Around 70,000 security personnel will be deployed on Saturday (October 31, 2026), matching the number mobilised a week ago, as authorities seek to avert a repeat of the October 17 unrest

France on Saturday (October 31, 2026) braced for a third weekend of protests coinciding with Halloween, as shops boarded up and authorities scrambled to prevent a repeat of the street violence that swept the country two weeks ago.
The demonstrations come in an increasingly febrile political climate, with presidential elections six months away and far-right leader Marine Le Pen leading opinion polls.
President Emmanuel Macron this week said it was "not normal" for France to be in such a state of "turmoil" so close to a presidential election.
Around 70,000 security personnel will be deployed on Saturday (October 31, 2026), matching the number mobilised a week ago, as authorities seek to avert a repeat of the October 17 unrest.
More than 40 metro stations will be closed in the capital and tram services will also be disrupted.

An aide to Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said they expected street violence on a scale "comparable" to the unrest two weeks ago, when images of clashes, looted shops and public buildings set ablaze were broadcast around the world.

The protest movement brings together Yellow Vest activists, trade unions, and high school and university students. It initially focused on the rising cost of living, inequality, and deteriorating learning conditions.
But following a security clampdown and serious injuries to some protesters, the movement broadened its demands to include greater protection of civil liberties and the right to protest.
A police source pointed to "considerable nervousness" among the authorities. "There is no reason to think this will go smoothly," the source said.
Alain Di Crescenzo, president of France's chamber of commerce, said business owners were worried.

TikTok and YouTube were also named as defendants in the case, but both had already reached settlements with the plaintiffs, known by their initials SJ and KDB, their lawyers said.
A California state judge consolidated the two cases into a single trial.
Snap, which makes Snapchat, will defend itself against the claims of both SJ and KDB.

The move comes ⁠as AI companies face growing scrutiny over the risks chatbots pose to young users and the companies’ ‌role in detecting threats of harm.
OpenAI will restrict practical ‌information on weapons and security systems that ‌could ⁠be misused , with the limits applying to ⁠teens even when there is no sign of violent intent
For all users, ChatGPT will be able to ​automatically end chats where ‌someone appears to be fixating on violence, and OpenAI may temporarily pause accounts after multiple such chats

The company also said ‌it strengthened its age prediction system to move ​users it estimates are under 18 into the teen experience, and it ⁠plans to notify parents if their teen’s account is paused for repeatedly discussing violence
For all ‌users, OpenAI is limiting detail on past mass attacks, including the weapons used and how they were obtained
The company said the new safeguards will begin rolling out in the next few weeks, and it will ‌continue to refine them
OpenAI said earlier this month ​that teens spend under 15 minutes a day on average on ChatGPT, in ⁠its first report on teen use

A report by ⁠non-profit Common Sense Media earlier this month found that ChatGPT’s teen version often ‌alerted parents late or not at all when teen accounts held conversations about suicide, self-harm ​or eating disorders

articles.title: A ferocious El Niño is brewing thanks to record Pacific heat
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Since the modern era of instrumental records began, there have only been three very strong El Niño events, in 2015-16, 1997-98, and 1982-83, with the three-month averages of the temperature anomaly being 2.6°, 2.4°, and 2.1°C, respectively. The 2026-27 El Niño is projected to peak with an anomaly of 3.8°C

For most of this year, climate scientists have been closely monitoring the Niño 3.4 region in the central-equatorial Pacific — the primary index area to define the phases of the El Niño Southern Oscillation and the alarming amount of ocean heat closely tracking an El Niño. The world’s oceans beyond the poles reached a record-high average surface temperature of 21.18°C on August 22, and daily sea surface temperatures in the Niño 3.4 region have been consistently shattering records.

According to the U.S. NOAA’s Climate Prediction Center, a ‘strong to very strong’ El Niño is 83% likely, with a high chance of a historic event exceeding the strength of any previous El Niño since 1950.

The El Niño is a natural climate pattern that emerges every two to seven years and affects global weather and heightens the risk of extreme heatwaves and altered rainfall worldwide. But this year’s event has put the world more on edge.

📰 A ferocious El Niño is brewing thanks to record Pacific heat

🎯 Exam Relevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Since the modern era of instrumental records began, there have only been three very strong El Niño events, in 2015-16, 1997-98, and 1982-83, with the three-month averages of the temperature anomaly being 2.6°, 2.4°, and 2.1°C, respectively. The 2026-27 El Niño is projected to peak with an anomaly of 3.8°C

For most of this year, climate scientists have been closely monitoring the Niño 3.4 region in the central-equatorial Pacific — the primary index area to define the phases of the El Niño Southern Oscillation and the alarming amount of ocean heat closely tracking an El Niño. The world’s oceans beyond the poles reached a record-high average surface temperature of 21.18°C on August 22, and daily sea surface temperatures in the Niño 3.4 region have been consistently shattering records.

According to the U.S. NOAA’s Climate Prediction Center, a ‘strong to very strong’ El Niño is 83% likely, with a high chance of a historic event exceeding the strength of any previous El Niño since 1950.

The El Niño is a natural climate pattern that emerges every two to seven years and affects global weather and heightens the risk of extreme heatwaves and altered rainfall worldwide. But this year’s event has put the world more on edge.

articles.title: Your DNA says less about your personality than a short online quiz
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The findings of new research reinforce a long-standing idea in genetics that there is no single ‘personality gene’; the dataset the researchers used also directly challenged older theories that attempted to link traits to particular brain chemicals

Decades of psychology have categorised human personality into five broad buckets: openness to experience (curiosity and imagination), conscientiousness (organisation and responsibility), extraversion (sociability), agreeableness (compassion), and neuroticism (a tendency towards anxiety and volatility).

In new findings published in Nature , scientists have completed one of the largest-ever genetic analyses of these ‘big five’ traits, offering a more detailed picture of the genetic architecture of personality.

“The finding that genetic signals were broadly consistent across different contexts … supports the view that personality traits such as extraversion and neuroticism have a biological basis,” Veena Kumari, professor of Experimental Psychology at Brunel University London, said. “However, like most psychological constructs, personality is a complex phenotype.” She noted that human behaviour remains deeply tethered to its environment and “may not be similarly expressed, or even measured with the same precision” across different walks of life.

articles.title: Inland waterway proposed to link Kottayam port with Vizhinjam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The 180-km journey from Kottayam to Vizhinjam is expected to take 12 to 14 hours. The waterway, with 17 bridges, maintains a depth of around 2 m, making it navigable for container barges.

In a move that could open up a new inland logistics route to Vizhinjam, Kottayam port has proposed a 180-km waterway corridor linking the country’s first inland container depot with the international seaport.

The proposal comes just months before the port is set to launch its barge service to Kochi. Discussions have already been held with the Industries Minister and officials of the Inland Waterways department, who have extended their support to the project. With the State government deciding to appoint the Ports Secretary as chairman of Kottayam port and the CEO of the Kerala Maritime Board as a member of its board, talks with Vizhinjam port authorities are also expected to gather pace. The port authorities are planning to discuss the proposal with Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan soon.
The project envisages transporting containers from Kottayam to Vizhinjam through National Waterways 9 and 3, before entering the Arabian Sea through the Valiyazheekkal breakwaters.

Located close to National Waterway 9, Kottayam port can connect to National Waterway 3 (Kollam-Kottappuram) through Munroe Island and Ashtamudi Lake. From there, barges can navigate the Pampa river, passing Ambalappuzha, Thottappally and Thrikkunnapuzha, before reaching Valiyazheekkal in Kayamkulam Lake. They can then enter the Arabian Sea and proceed to Vizhinjam.

The 180-km journey from Kottayam to Vizhinjam is expected to take 12 to 14 hours. The route has 17 bridges, with a major lock system scheduled to be installed at the Thrikkunnapuzha bridge by December. This will allow container barges to pass through without difficulty. The waterway maintains a depth of around two metres along the route, making it navigable for barges.

“A preliminary survey has been completed, while the secondary survey is expected to begin by January next year after consultations with the State government. The project will not involve any significant expenditure for the government. A foreign investor has expressed willingness to invest ₹100 crore in the port in four instalments. A portion of this will be used to build a barge for transporting containers to Vizhinjam,” a senior port official said.
Besides procuring a new barge, the investment will be used to expand the port’s infrastructure, including the development of a paved yard and the installation of a crane, berth and reach stacker.

Meanwhile, the port has already begun moving containers to Vizhinjam under a transshipment bond arrangement with the Customs Department. The arrangement allows goods to be cleared at Kottayam before being transported to Vizhinjam, helping businesses save both time and money.

articles.title: Depression over Bay of Bengal may bring rain to Telangana, heavy showers likely in nine districts on November 2
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The system would weaken considerably before reaching Telangana, says S. Stella, Head of the IMD Centre Hyderabad

The second depression over the southeast Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a cyclonic storm before moving towards the Andhra Pradesh coast, but it is likely to weaken into a deep depression by the time it reaches Telangana, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD).

The system is expected to move west-northwestwards and cross the Andhra Pradesh coast on the morning of November 3. While the system is forecast to intensify into a cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal, its intensity is expected to reduce as it moves inland.

Speaking to The Hindu , S. Stella, Head of the IMD Centre Hyderabad said the system would weaken considerably before reaching Telangana and that the State was unlikely to experience the impact of a cyclonic storm. “It will be a depression only. It will weaken. Moreover, when it is weakening, the clouds and all will shear off,” she said.
According to her, Telangana is likely to receive light to moderate rainfall from November 2 to 4, with isolated heavy rainfall at few places on November 3 and 4.

On November 2, heavy rainfall is very likely to occur at isolated places in Adilabad, Kumaram Bheem Asifabad, Mancherial, Jagtial, Mahabubnagar, Nagarkurnool, Wanaparthy, Narayanpet and Jogulamba Gadwal districts. On November 3, heavy rainfall is very likely to occur at isolated places in Mahabubnagar, Nagarkurnool, Wanaparthy, Narayanpet and Jogulamba Gadwal districts. Hyderabad, too, is likely to receive light to moderate rainfall during this period, Ms. Stella added.

The IMD’s observed and forecast track, based on observations at 11.30 a.m. on Saturday (October 31, 2026), shows the depression moving west-northwestwards from the southeast Bay of Bengal. It is expected to strengthen into a deep depression by the evening of October 31, followed by a cyclonic storm over the subsequent 24 hours. The system is likely to reach the Andhra Pradesh coast on November 2 before moving inland towards Telangana.

The system would weaken considerably before reaching Telangana, says S. Stella, Head of the IMD Centre Hyderabad

The second depression over the southeast Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a cyclonic storm before moving towards the Andhra Pradesh coast, but it is likely to weaken into a deep depression by the time it reaches Telangana, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD).

The system is expected to move west-northwestwards and cross the Andhra Pradesh coast on the morning of November 3. While the system is forecast to intensify into a cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal, its intensity is expected to reduce as it moves inland.

Speaking to The Hindu , S. Stella, Head of the IMD Centre Hyderabad said the system would weaken considerably before reaching Telangana and that the State was unlikely to experience the impact of a cyclonic storm. “It will be a depression only. It will weaken. Moreover, when it is weakening, the clouds and all will shear off,” she said.

According to her, Telangana is likely to receive light to moderate rainfall from November 2 to 4, with isolated heavy rainfall at few places on November 3 and 4.

On November 2, heavy rainfall is very likely to occur at isolated places in Adilabad, Kumaram Bheem Asifabad, Mancherial, Jagtial, Mahabubnagar, Nagarkurnool, Wanaparthy, Narayanpet and Jogulamba Gadwal districts. On November 3, heavy rainfall is very likely to occur at isolated places in Mahabubnagar, Nagarkurnool, Wanaparthy, Narayanpet and Jogulamba Gadwal districts. Hyderabad, too, is likely to receive light to moderate rainfall during this period, Ms. Stella added.

The IMD’s observed and forecast track, based on observations at 11.30 a.m. on Saturday (October 31, 2026), shows the depression moving west-northwestwards from the southeast Bay of Bengal. It is expected to strengthen into a deep depression by the evening of October 31, followed by a cyclonic storm over the subsequent 24 hours. The system is likely to reach the Andhra Pradesh coast on November 2 before moving inland towards Telangana.

articles.title: Census 2027: J&K completes DCHB fieldwork; population enumeration training underway
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Sharma said the data collected during the exercise would now undergo scrutiny and validation. Charge Officers have been given 15 days to recheck and compile the information, which is expected to reach the Directorate by November 15

Jammu and Kashmir has completed 100% fieldwork for the District Census Handbook (DCHB), covering 6,466 villages and 80 towns across the Union Territory, Director Census Amit Sharma said on Saturday (October 31, 2026).

He said preparations for the Population Enumeration exercise in the non-snowbound areas were underway, with a series of training programmes for Census personnel scheduled between October 26 and January 2027, ahead of the actual exercise beginning on January 25.

"The DCHB exercise, conducted from October 8 to 30, had been successfully completed across Jammu and Kashmir. A total of 6,466 villages and 80 towns have been covered, with 100% completion of fieldwork," Mr. Sharma, who is also the Chief Principal Census Officer of J&K and Ladakh, told reporters in Jammu.

He said the DCHB, comprising the Village Directory and Town Directory, documents the availability of essential facilities and infrastructure, including educational and healthcare institutions, drinking water, sanitation, electricity, banking, communication, irrigation, agriculture and other civic amenities.

Mr. Sharma said the data collected during the exercise would now undergo scrutiny and validation. Charge Officers have been given 15 days to recheck and compile the information, which is expected to reach the Directorate by November 15.

The Directorate will subsequently undertake a detailed evaluation and scrutiny of the data, which is expected to be completed by December 15. The finalised information will then be forwarded to the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India for publication, the Director said.

Turning to preparations for Population Enumeration, Mr. Sharma said the exercise in the snowbound areas of Jammu and Kashmir had been completed during September, covering snowbound areas of 16 districts.

While Kishtwar district was covered entirely, the snowbound areas of the remaining 15 districts were covered partially. Special Charges, including personnel of the armed forces and other security establishments, were also covered during the exercise, he said.
Mr. Sharma said preparations for Population Enumeration in the non-snowbound and plain areas were now underway in full swing.

The Government of India had notified the schedule for Population Enumeration, under which self-enumeration would be conducted from January 10 to 24, followed by fieldwork from January 25 to February 28, he said.

articles.title: Kharge moves six charges against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, says 'no personal enmity', BJP accuses Congress of mocking Parliament | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: INDIA Bloc says everyone united in protests, 'public impeachment' of CEC Gyanesh Kumar today

Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge outlined six allegations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in the INDIA bloc’s public impeachment resolution, accusing him of facilitating alleged vote theft, deleting 13.2 crore voter names, changing Form 6 and acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Amit Shah.

peaking at the INDIA bloc’s symbolic impeachment programme against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi, TMC MP Saugata Roy said the Opposition had followed legal procedure to submit an impeachment notice but was not allowed to raise the issue in Parliament. He also cited concerns over voter names being deleted from electoral rolls.

RJD leader and Bihar Leader of Opposition Tejashwi Yadav accused Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of orchestrating alleged vote theft at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Amit Shah. He vowed to unite against what he described as an attempt to undermine democracy.

BJP MP Sambit Patra defended the voter registration process amid the SIR row, asserting that only Indian citizens should vote and urging those whose names are missing from electoral rolls to submit Form 6. He said a declaration form had been added, but Form 6 itself remained unchanged.

BJP MP Sambit Patra criticised the Congress’s symbolic ‘mock Parliament’ protest, alleging that the first instance of vote theft took place under Jawaharlal Nehru. He also defended the SIR process, explaining the ‘ASDD’ categories used to identify voters missing from electoral rolls.

Addressing the INDIA bloc’s symbolic impeachment programme in New Delhi, Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge accused Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of acting against the Constitution and demanded his immediate removal and trial for treason.

Mallikarjun Kharge said the INDIA bloc was not fighting to protect “infiltrators” but for genuine voters, as he spoke at its symbolic ‘public impeachment’ of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar today (October 31, 2026).

The six charges displayed at the event allege that the CEC conspired to steal elections, deleted 13.2 crore voters, rewrote Form 6 without Parliament, seized the electoral rolls through ECINET, shut out the other two Election Commissioners, and acted at the behest of Narendra Modi and Amit Shah.

Ahead of the planned Congress-led INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1, 2026, the Delhi Police have said traffic restrictions will be in place across parts of the national capital from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Sunday.
The traffic police have listed key diversions in Central Delhi, likely regulations on bus movements and suggested alternate routes to reach the New Delhi Railway Station.

articles.title: How significant is the TVK-led regime’s move to hold Social Justice Survey? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The feature of an ‘open column’, where respondents can state their caste during the second phase of the Census, to be carried out in most parts of the country during February next year, has forced many parties and other stakeholders to express concerns over the utility of the whole exercise

The story so far: The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) -led regime, headed by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, at a Cabinet meeting in Chennai on Thursday (October 29, 2026), formally gave its nod to constitute a multi-member panel to conduct what the government called the Social Justice Survey. This was in tune with the announcement made by Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar in his address to the Assembly in June last that once the Union Government completed the caste enumeration, the State government would conduct the Social Justice Survey.

Political parties, across the spectrum, have been demanding that a caste census or survey be undertaken. However, there have been differences in the approach to the exercise. The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) , the principal Opposition party in the Assembly, while in power during 2021-26, took the stand that the Caste Census be carried out along with the general Census. However, its traditional adversary, the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) , during its regime in 2020, formed a commission, headed by a former judge of the Madras High Court, to work out the methodologies for collecting caste-wise data and following them up with a survey. But its tenure, when it came to an end in June 2021, was not renewed by the successor DMK government. In the meantime, the Union government had announced that caste would be counted during the Population Census 2027, involving the collection of demographic, socio-economic, cultural and other details.

articles.title: Petrol export duty cut to nil, diesel levy raised by ₹3 a litre
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The government’s fortnightly review raised the export levy on diesel to ₹11.5 per litre from ₹8.5 and on aviation turbine fuel to ₹11 per litre from ₹10.5, while India’s diesel exports touched 700 kilo barrels per day in October, the highest since September 2025, according to Kpler

articles.title: France heads into third weekend of protests as youth-led rallies sweep Europe
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez warned of a “very high risk” of disorder, especially after dark on Halloween

France prepared on Saturday (October 31, 2026) for a third consecutive weekend of protests over living costs and education, deploying 70,000 police and gendarmes and rerouting the Paris march to the capital's edge as youth-led demonstrations spread across Europe.
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez warned of a “very high risk” of disorder, especially after dark on Halloween.

Paris police banned union and “yellow vest” marches through the city centre, ordering demonstrations to follow a single route along the capital's outer boulevards, from Porte de Bagnolet to Porte de Charenton. Unions and student groups challenged the restrictions in court, but lost.
President Emmanuel Macron said on Monday (October 26, 2026) that marches would stay out of city centres to protect shops.
Police also barred entry to Place de la Republique and Les Halles, both hit by rioting and looting on October 17, from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. on Saturday (October 31, 2026) and Sunday (November 1, 2026).

Unaccompanied minors face a separate 9 p.m. curfew around the Champs-Elysees. A Paris court on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) suspended an earlier curfew on minors as a serious and illegal infringement of freedom of movement.
The movement began with high school students protesting school conditions and broadened into anger over living costs.

Authorities counted about 550,000 protesters nationwide on October 17, when rioters looted hundreds of shops, and 410,000 last Saturday (October 31, 2026), when rallies were largely peaceful but police made more than 1,300 arrests.

In Germany, a youth initiative called “Gen Z regelt” — roughly “Gen Z's got this” — urged protests in some 30 cities “for education, health, climate protection and an affordable life,” and against any return of military conscription. Organisers said more than 140,000 people had signed up online.

Berlin police expected about 10,000 people at the Brandenburg Gate. Some shops on the Kurfuerstendamm boulevard boarded up their windows, although authorities said they were unaware of specific threats of violence. Protests were expected to begin in the early afternoon.

articles.title: Britain open to apologising for slavery, says Andy Burnham
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Mr. Burnham pushed back against the notion of financial reparations for victims of slavery saying that the British people could not be held responsible for historical wrongs; Burnham’s omission of colonialism ‘inexcusable’, said Tharoor
U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said his government is open to the idea of formally apologising for Britain’s historical role in the slave trade, although he ruled out financial reparations.

Mr. Burnham set out his position in an opinion piece in The Guardian on Friday (October 30, 2026), ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) in Antigua and Barbuda, next week. There have, for long, been calls for Britain to apologise and offer reparations for slavery and its colonial past, including in India.

Some three million Africans were transported as slaves to work on plantations in Britian’s colonies in the Americas. Britain began abolishing the slave trade in its empire in 1807. Slavery was abolished in 1833 though not all slaves were freed until 1838. Britain “compensated” slave owners to a total sum of GBP 20 million or 40% of the government’s annual budget in 1833.
“Manchester’s cotton industry was built on the labour of enslaved people,” wrote Mr. Burnham, the former Mayor of Manchester.
Mr. Burnham acknowledged the calls from affected countries for a dialogue on slavery.

“By sticking our heads in the sand, we have damaged the ability of the Commonwealth to function,” he said, adding that it was necessary to have conversations on slavery to protect the future of the Commonwealth.
Mr. Burnham said the U.K. was “offering structured dialogue with those affected by the transatlantic slave trade”.
“Listening to calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British state will form an important part of this process, and I am open to them,” he added.

Calls for Britain to make amends for its past have grown louder in recent days as Britain’s King Charles III tours the Caribbean on his way to the CHOGM. The King is the titular head of the Commonwealth.
In the Bahamas this week, Charles acknowledged the “great suffering and injustices of the past”, stopping short of an apology.

📰 Britain open to apologising for slavery, says Andy Burnham

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Mr. Burnham pushed back against the notion of financial reparations for victims of slavery saying that the British people could not be held responsible for historical wrongs; Burnham’s omission of colonialism ‘inexcusable’, said Tharoor

U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said his government is open to the idea of formally apologising for Britain’s historical role in the slave trade, although he ruled out financial reparations.

Mr. Burnham set out his position in an opinion piece in The Guardian on Friday (October 30, 2026), ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) in Antigua and Barbuda, next week. There have, for long, been calls for Britain to apologise and offer reparations for slavery and its colonial past, including in India.

Some three million Africans were transported as slaves to work on plantations in Britian’s colonies in the Americas. Britain began abolishing the slave trade in its empire in 1807. Slavery was abolished in 1833 though not all slaves were freed until 1838. Britain “compensated” slave owners to a total sum of GBP 20 million or 40% of the government’s annual budget in 1833.

“Manchester’s cotton industry was built on the labour of enslaved people,” wrote Mr. Burnham, the former Mayor of Manchester.

Mr. Burnham acknowledged the calls from affected countries for a dialogue on slavery.

“By sticking our heads in the sand, we have damaged the ability of the Commonwealth to function,” he said, adding that it was necessary to have conversations on slavery to protect the future of the Commonwealth.

Mr. Burnham said the U.K. was “offering structured dialogue with those affected by the transatlantic slave trade”.

“Listening to calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British state will form an important part of this process, and I am open to them,” he added.

Calls for Britain to make amends for its past have grown louder in recent days as Britain’s King Charles III tours the Caribbean on his way to the CHOGM. The King is the titular head of the Commonwealth.

In the Bahamas this week, Charles acknowledged the “great suffering and injustices of the past”, stopping short of an apology.

1. Core Context & Background: Mr. Burnham pushed back against the notion of financial reparations for victims of slavery saying that the British people could not be held responsible for historical wrongs; Burnham’s omission of colonialism ‘inexcusable’, said Tharoor

articles.title: Saudi Arabia says intercepted ‘hostile drone’ in Riyadh region
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: No information yet on who launched the drone
Saudi air defences intercepted a drone in the Riyadh region on Saturday (October 31, 2026), according to the spokesman for the Saudi-led military coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis.
"Air defences intercepted and destroyed a hostile drone in the Riyadh region," Turki al-Malki wrote on X, adding that "debris from the interception fell without causing injuries".

In recent weeks, Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis have ramped up attacks on Saudi Arabia, including by launching deadly strikes on Riyadh airport that forced its closure for two weeks and the cancellation of flagship events — threatening the kingdom's economic diversification plans.
On Friday (October 30, 2026), Mr. Malki said the Houthis had targeted the Medina region, home to Islam's second holiest city, but the group later denied the claim.

The Houthi attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure, airports and ships come after hostilities resumed in Yemen over the summer between the Houthis and the country's internationally recognised government, which is backed by Riyadh.

articles.title: Nations commit to get nature goals back on track at UN nature summit
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The United Nations had warned that progress was insufficient to meet the goals of the 2030 target including protecting 30% of Earth’s land and oceans, tackling pollution and invasive species, and boosting money for conservation

Nearly 200 nations struck hard-fought agreements on Friday (October 30, 2026) at a UN biodiversity summit, but the outcome was accompanied by disappointment over missed opportunities to address humanity’s destructive toll on nature.
Delegates cheered as crucial texts were approved in overtime but the celebrations were tempered by acrimonious debates and regret over limited progress on some of the most contentious issues.
The COP17 summit in Armenia sought to revive a landmark commitment to halt and reverse the destruction of nature by 2030 after global efforts to meet that goal fell short.
Over two bruising weeks in Yerevan, nations were urged to correct course to keep the pact alive and protect the plants, animals and ecosystems that sustain life on Earth.

The United Nations had warned that progress was insufficient to meet the goals of the 2030 target including protecting 30% of Earth’s land and oceans, tackling pollution and invasive species, and boosting money for conservation.

“And that’s it. Perfect,” said COP17 president Hambardzum Matevosyan in Armenia as he brought down the gavel on two major texts, the final versions of which were still not available early on Saturday (October 31).

But the outcome was “not commensurate” with the crisis engulfing the natural world, said French Ecological Transition Minister Monique Barbut early on Saturday (October 31) as the summit drew to a close.

“The progress we failed to achieve here is a series of missed opportunities to speed up our response to the loss of biodiversity,” Ms. Barbut said in a lengthy statement sent to AFP , stressing that “nature will not wait for the pace of our negotiations.”
The final plenary stretched through Friday (October 30) night and well into the next morning, with negotiations turning sour as the hours dragged on.
Even as some delegates left to catch flights, others stayed behind to argue technical points.

articles.title: ISRO NVS-03 launch: 5 things to know about India’s new navigation satellite
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: ISRO successfully launched the NVS-03 navigation satellite from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota on October 30, 2026, restoring NavIC to a four-satellite, standalone operational status and advancing India’s push for an indigenous, more precise space-time network

India’s independent regional navigation satellite system NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation) was restored to its minimum operational configuration of four satellites on Friday (October 30, 2026) as ISRO successfully launched its 2,250 kg navigation satellite NVS-03 from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota.

The satellite successfully separated from the launch vehicle and was injected into its intended Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO). The satellite is the third in ISRO's next-generation navigation satellite series, envisaged to ensure continuity of navigation services under the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS). This mission aims to revive and modernise NavIC.
Here’s what to know about India’s new navigation satellite, NVS-03, with a mission life of 12 years.

NavIC requires at least 4 active satellites to provide positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) services. Following clock failures on older satellites and failure of NVS-02 to reach its final orbit, the operational fleet shrank to just 3 satellites. Placing NVS-03 into orbit provided the fourth satellite needed to restore standalone navigation services.
Atomic clocks are central to satellite navigation and helps calculate exact distances by measuring signal travel time.

Older IRNSS satellites relied on imported Swiss clocks that repeatedly failed. NVS-03 carries a indigenously developed Rubidium atomic clock (developed by ISRO’s Space Applications Centre) alongside imported ones. This moves India closer to full self reliance in high precision space timing.

NVS-03 transmits on the L1 frequency band in addition to the existing L5 and S bands. The L1 band is widely used in commercial GPS receivers, which will make it easier for everyday mobile chipsets to access Indian Standard Time and NavIC positioning signals. The system is designed to provide coverage over India’s landmass and an area extending 1,500 kilometres beyond its geopolitical boundary.
NavIC offers two main services: an open signal for public navigation, mapping and logistics, and an encrypted restricted service for the military.
The latter provides high-precision data essential for guiding missiles, tracking troop movements and operating defence platforms safely, practically acting as a strategic asset for India.

Elaborating on NavIC’s civilian applications, the ISRO chief V. Narayanan said 10,400 locomotives and 64,000 fishing vessels are currently tracked in real time. Under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana, the agency aims to expand this to 1 lakh fishing vessels within the next six months. In total, 15 lakh tracking devices have been fitted across vehicles. When asked when NavIC would be available on civilian mobile phones, Narayanan stated this would happen once the full seven-satellite constellation is completed.

The satellite is the third in ISRO's next-generation navigation satellite series, envisaged to ensure continuity of navigation services under the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS). This mission aims to revive and modernise NavIC.

fullParagraphs: Across their lifespans, from childhood to old age, women face disadvantages in access to eye health and care. For many, treatment depends on how their health is prioritised by the men in their household. Late care, or lack of access can leave girls and women with preventable visual impairment and loss

“I remember a patient, a little girl with retinoblastoma,” says Rohit Khanna, a community ophthalmologist and network director from L.V. Prasad Eye Institute, Hyderabad. “We told the family that the child required surgery and that the eyeball would have to be removed for her to survive. We were immediately met with resistance. The father asked, what was the point of her living if she was going to be disfigured. They would not be able to get her married later.”

articles.title: AI giants promise publishers new way to block some
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Publishers currently have to implement multiple blocking commands for every that crawls the web to collect data

OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic pledged on Friday to give media outlets and other websites a single way to prevent their content from being to train artificial intelligence (AI) models, amid growing criticisms and legal battles from news publishers.

Publishers currently have to implement multiple blocking commands for every that crawls the web to collect data , but the new proposed solution will allow them to enter a single, standardized instruction that's recognized and honored by any AI company that adopts the protocol.
The solution will not fully take effect for months, though.

Microsoft will implement it beginning February 1, 2027, and Google sometime in 2027. ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said it will roll it out "in the coming months," while Claude-maker Anthropic said it has "already started" rolling it out.
The announcement comes as publishers are facing a surge in bots that scrape their articles to feed AI models. Some, like the New York Times, have taken the matter to court.

Meanwhile, internet infrastructure provider Cloudflare has blocked AI bots by default on new customer sites since July 2025, and a standard called Really Simple Licensing already allows publishers to charge bots that visit their pages.

The new setting will apply only to future training of models but does not prevent bots from crawling otherwise, and content will be allowed by default until the setting is changed by a publisher, Microsoft said in a blog post.
Opting out of AI training could reduce the chances that a publisher's content will surface in AI apps and experiences, Microsoft and Google said in separate blog posts.

"We believe creating a common signal that conveys such preferences to multiple providers at once is an important step. And we look forward to working with other AI companies on the standards and their implementation across the industry," Meta spokesperson Andy Stone wrote on X, conveying his support for the effort.

articles.title: Revanth Reddy resorting to ‘credit chori’ in land cases fought by BRS govt.: Harish Rao
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Senior leader of Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) T. Harish Rao has termed Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy taking credit for the Miyapur lands case win in the Supreme Court as “credit chori”.

Addressing a press conference here on Saturday, he said it was the BRS Government till 2023 that had won many land cases in court to protect government lands. He alleged that the Chief Minister was after the District Collector concerned for sale of 550 acres lands in Miyapur even before he got a copy of the Supreme Court judgment.
Of the 192 hearings in the Miyapur lands case, 86 were argued by C.S. Vaidyanathan, appointed by the BRS Government, and only 11 hearings had taken place after the Congress had come to power.

He alleged that the previous Congress Government weakened the Greyhounds land case of Manchirevulu in 2010 by sending a Government Pleader to argue the case instead of the Advocate General. On May 19, 2017, the KCR Government filed an appeal and a High Court Division Bench gave its judgment in the government’s favour on December 31, 2021. The Supreme Court had given the final verdict in the 142 acres land case on August 1, 2023, to secure the land to Greyhounds.

The 30-year-old compound wall of Greyhounds facility was demolished overnight, and within two days, a new compound wall was constructed after leaving 10.10 acres of land to private persons. It was also shown as zero-value registration land in the Gandipet SRO document 8886/2026 when the land value was ₹45.39 crore, he claimed.

He alleged that it was registered in the name of Dream Valley (Santosh Reddy) without payment of the 7.5% registration fee. Later, another 20 registrations were done to take ₹1,000 crore worth of government land. The land was still in the name of Greyhounds (Police Department) in the Bhu Bharathi records.

The Revanth Reddy Government had not even appealed against the cancellation of the notification on another 10 acres land acquired for the Greyhounds Firing Range. The total value of the Manchirevulu land scam was about ₹2,000 crore, the BRS leader stated and added that it was the BRS Government that had sent Goldstone Prasad to jail.

articles.title: India-linked Buddha relics to be enshrined in 108 chortens in Bhutan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The simultaneous raising of these stupas will mark the spiritual foundation of Gelephu Mindfulness City, envisioned as a spirituality-driven global economic hub; this is a test of national character, says King Jigme Wangchuk

Buddhist relics of Indian origin will be enshrined in most of the 108 jangchub chortens (stupas of enlightenment) that monks and volunteers are scheduled to build simultaneously along a 12 km stretch of the Mau Chhu River in the Bhutanese town of Gelephu on Sunday (November 1, 2026).

The event will mark the spiritual foundation of the Gelephu Mindfulness City (GMC), which Bhutan’s King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuk envisions as a spirituality-driven global economic hub. About 240 km south-southeast of Bhutan’s capital, Thimphu, the city borders Assam’s Chirang district.

The Central Monastic Body of Bhutan, the country’s principal institutional carrier of the Drukpa Kagyu lineage of Tibetan Buddhism, said that Buddhists in Malaysia, Singapore, Taiwan, Thailand, and Bhutan had donated hundreds of relics, mostly bones and hair.

“Malaysia sent three sets of 108 relics of the Buddha, enlightened saints and revered lamas. We received many from Thailand. Most of the relics were established as having been sourced from India,” Choten Dorji, the Principal Secretary to one of the masters of the monastic body, said on Saturday (October 31, 2026).
The royal gallery at Gelephu Mindfulness City, on October 31, 2026 | Photo Credit: Rahul Karmakar

The relics form part of the ‘ zung ’, the living embodiment of the Buddha’s enlightened body, speech and mind. The sacred components of the zung include thangkhas (traditional Tibetan Buddhist paintings on cotton or silk fabric), statues, precious stones, rolled mantra scrolls, or dharanis , and relics of enlightened beings.

The jangchub chorten commemorates the Buddha’s attainment of enlightenment and symbolises the triumph of wisdom over ignorance. Once consecrated, a chorten is rendered equivalent to the living Buddha.
On February 26, King Wangchuk announced Project 108 at the GMC as a “test of national character”, not merely an initiative to set a world record.

“It is an ambitious undertaking that demands courage, unity, and deep commitment. We must do it to prove to ourselves that, as we face the challenges ahead, there is no limit to what we can achieve when we stand together,” he said.
Volunteers line up for work at the main venue of Project 108 Jangchub Chortens on October 31, 2026 | Photo Credit: Rahul Karmakar

articles.title: Prajaseva special drive facilitates e-Khata for 590 owners
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Mysuru City Corporation (MCC) issued e-khata certificates to 590 eligible applicants on Saturday, the concluding day of its three-day Prajaseva e-Aasthi special campaign.
Of 730 applications received on October 28, 590 applications submitted along with necessary documents were found eligible for receiving e-khata.

The MCC has decided to conduct another drive on November 5, 6 and 7 to provide another opportunity for eligible property owners within its limits to secure e-khata certificates. Those who could not take part in the campaign this month or failed to submit essential documents can avail this opportunity, a press release from MCC said.
The MCC limits cover more than 2.10 lakh properties, of which e-khata certificates have been issued to over 78,700 property owners.

Officials have been directed to expedite the issuance of e-khata certificates to the remaining eligible property owners, said Minister in-charge of Mysuru district Yathindra Siddharamaiah, who symbolically distributed e-khata certificates to the property owners at a programme organised by the MCC as part of the Prajaseva campaign.

Expressing happiness over the enthusiastic public participation to e-khata special drive, the Minister urged property owners to utilise the opportunity and submit applications along with the required documents. He directed officials to prioritise verification of eligible applications and issuance of e-katha certificates in accordance with the rules.
MLA Tanveer Sait, Deputy Commissioner G. Lakshmikanth Reddy, Regional Commissioner Nitesh Patil, MCC Commissioner Savitha, Zilla Panchayat CEO Yukesh Kumar, and other officials were present.

articles.title: Sugarcane growers intensify agitation across Kittur Karnataka; bandh evokes mixed response; Road blockades disrupt transport in Belagavi, Vijayapura, Bagalkot, Dharwad and Haveri
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Karnataka bandh called by sugarcane growers demanding a remunerative price for their produce evoked a mixed response across the Kittur Karnataka region on Saturday, with road blockades disrupting transport and normal life in several parts of Belagavi, Vijayapura, Bagalkot, Dharwad and Haveri districts.

The growers are demanding ₹5,500 a tonne for sugarcane, including an incentive of ₹1,000 a tonne from the State government. They have also urged the Union government to increase the minimum selling price (MSP) of sugar from ₹31 to ₹60 a kg.

In Belagavi, the bandh evoked a moderate response in the city but had a wider impact in rural areas. Farmers belonging to the Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha and Hasiru Sene staged a protest at the Central Bus Stand from 6 a.m. to 8 a.m., disrupting bus services. Commercial activity returned to normal around 9 a.m.

Road blockades continued in Gokak, Kagwad, Yaragatti, Hukkeri, Nipani, Mudalagi, Athani and other towns. Farmers blocked roads connecting Karnataka and Maharashtra near Nipani and Kagwad. At Gokak, protesters blocked the Gokak-Hidkal Dam road and prepared food on the highway. At Ugaragol in Savadatti taluk, a blockade on the road to the Renuka Yellamma temple forced devotees to return without darshan.

In Dharwad, growers blocked the main road near Jubilee Circle for more than two hours, bringing traffic to a standstill. Chigari and State transport bus services were temporarily suspended. Police Commissioner Bhushan Borase visited the spot and persuaded the protesters to clear the road. The blockade was withdrawn around 1 p.m. Hubballi too witnessed traffic disruptions because of protest by farmers. Several shops and commercial establishments r

Haveri witnessed a mixed response amid tense scenes. Farmers began a round-the-clock sit-in outside Sugar Minister Rudrappa Lamani’s residence, erecting a shamiana on the road. The Minister was in Bengaluru, while police barricaded the approach roads.

Protesters urged traders to close their establishments, leading to heated exchanges near Siddappa Circle and the district bus stand. Transport was also affected after farmers blocked the Ilkal-Shikaripura highway near Chowdayyadanapur. Buses were stranded at Guttal and services at the Haveri bus stand were disrupted.

Vijayapura district witnessed a strong response. Babaleshwar observed a complete bandh, while farmers blocked the Vijayapura-Pandharpur highway at Siddapur. At Sangapur S.H. village, protesters surrounded Industries Minister M.B. Patil and demanded his intervention. An argument followed, prompting the police to use lathis to disperse the crowd. Farmers alleged that police personnel had abused and assaulted them.
In Vijayapura city, farmers blocked the Hitnalli toll plaza for nearly two hours. Muddebihal also observed a complete bandh. The agitation received support in several other taluks.
Bagalkot district witnessed a good response, while Gadag saw only symbolic protests.

fullParagraphs: Mr. Burnham pushed back against the notion of financial reparations for victims of slavery saying that the British people could not be held responsible for historical wrongs; Burnham’s omission of colonialism ‘inexcusable’, said Tharoor
U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said his government is open to the idea of formally apologising for Britain’s historical role in the slave trade, although he ruled out financial reparations.

articles.title: India’s first fusion power company takes key steps
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Designs for the first privately built tokamak, a nuclear reactor that uses fusion to produce energy, could be firmed up in 2027 by Bengaluru-based startup Pranos Fusion
If all goes to plan, India may see designs for the first privately built tokamak, a nuclear reactor that uses fusion to produce energy, firmed up in 2027.

Bengaluru-based startup Pranos Fusion has built PRAGYA, a small doughnut shaped tokamak, to test plasma control and superconducting magnets. This is a gateway to building PRANIK, a much larger tokomak that will have plasma heated up to millions of degrees — more than the interior of the Sun — necessary to fuse hydrogen atoms and create energy.

“By 2027, we expect to finalise the blueprint for PRANIK and be on our way to building a practical reactor that can produce energy. To be able to actually produce electricity from fusion is a further step away,” Shaurya Kaushal, co-founder and CEO of Pranos Fusion, said.

The company is currently incubated out of the Institute of Plasma Research, a body affiliated to the Department of Atomic Energy and the Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research (JNCASR), Bengaluru, an institute with the Department of Science and Technology.

Nuclear plants everywhere employ fission — a chain reaction involving uranium nuclei to produce heat that is used to generate electricity. Fusion, on the other hand, releases energy when light atomic nuclei merge, and usually involves joining two forms of hydrogen — deuterium and tritium — into helium and a fast neutron. However, this requires the fuel to be heated to around 100 million degrees Celsius, far hotter than any solid wall could withstand. In tokamaks, powerful magnets hold this superheated plasma away from the walls, keeping it hot enough for fusion to continue.
Pranos Fusion was one of the deeptech startups showcased at the Emerging Science Technology and Innovation Conclave held here last week.

“Electricity from a fusion reactor is still far away and would be expensive now, however the need for any source of energy is only going to grow,” Roshan George, co-founder and a Computer Science engineer from the Manipal Institute of Technology. “Fusion’s advantage is that while [it’s] nuclear power, it doesn’t need radioactive material like uranium. India already produces plenty of deuterium. Fusion reactions are also not chain reactions, and therefore the risk of a runaway reaction [like in a fission reactor] is almost absent,” Mr. George said.

The largest tokamak under construction is the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor in southern France, a collaboration between China, the European Union, India, Japan, Russia, South Korea, and the U.S. It is designed to produce about 10 times the heating power fed into its plasma. Bogged by delays, a 2024 revision moved the start of research operations to 2034 and full deuterium-tritium operation to 2039, adding about €5 billion to the cost. IPR manages India’s home-grown tokamak reactors, including ADITYA and the Steady State Tokamak (SST-1). It is also the nodal domestic agency to manage India’s contributions to International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor.

The cost of a private tokamak depends on scale, Mr. Kaushal, who holds a Ph.D. from JNCASR, and a mechanical engineering degree from BITS Pilani, said. A compact research machine like PRAGYA is “a comparatively modest investment”, while one designed to reach net energy gain is far larger. Private fusion companies worldwide have raised over $13 billion, he said, and the leading net-gain programmes have each raised hundreds of millions of dollars or more.

Pranos Fusion says compact machines, HTS (high-temperature superconducting) magnets, and India’s manufacturing base can bring costs down substantially. It is backed by Ankur Capital, pi Ventures and Industrial47, and has raised $7.2 million. HTS electromagnets are wound from materials that carry electric current with no resistance when cooled below a critical temperature.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment 📅 31 Oct 2026 ⏱️ 5 Min Read

📰 India’s first fusion power company takes key steps

🎯 Exam Relevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Designs for the first privately built tokamak, a nuclear reactor that uses fusion to produce energy, could be firmed up in 2027 by Bengaluru-based startup Pranos Fusion

If all goes to plan, India may see designs for the first privately built tokamak, a nuclear reactor that uses fusion to produce energy, firmed up in 2027.

Bengaluru-based startup Pranos Fusion has built PRAGYA, a small doughnut shaped tokamak, to test plasma control and superconducting magnets. This is a gateway to building PRANIK, a much larger tokomak that will have plasma heated up to millions of degrees — more than the interior of the Sun — necessary to fuse hydrogen atoms and create energy.

“By 2027, we expect to finalise the blueprint for PRANIK and be on our way to building a practical reactor that can produce energy. To be able to actually produce electricity from fusion is a further step away,” Shaurya Kaushal, co-founder and CEO of Pranos Fusion, said.

The company is currently incubated out of the Institute of Plasma Research, a body affiliated to the Department of Atomic Energy and the Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research (JNCASR), Bengaluru, an institute with the Department of Science and Technology.

Nuclear plants everywhere employ fission — a chain reaction involving uranium nuclei to produce heat that is used to generate electricity. Fusion, on the other hand, releases energy when light atomic nuclei merge, and usually involves joining two forms of hydrogen — deuterium and tritium — into helium and a fast neutron. However, this requires the fuel to be heated to around 100 million degrees Celsius, far hotter than any solid wall could withstand. In tokamaks, powerful magnets hold this superheated plasma away from the walls, keeping it hot enough for fusion to continue.

Pranos Fusion was one of the deeptech startups showcased at the Emerging Science Technology and Innovation Conclave held here last week.

“Electricity from a fusion reactor is still far away and would be expensive now, however the need for any source of energy is only going to grow,” Roshan George, co-founder and a Computer Science engineer from the Manipal Institute of Technology. “Fusion’s advantage is that while [it’s] nuclear power, it doesn’t need radioactive material like uranium. India already produces plenty of deuterium. Fusion reactions are also not chain reactions, and therefore the risk of a runaway reaction [like in a fission reactor] is almost absent,” Mr. George said.

The largest tokamak under construction is the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor in southern France, a collaboration between China, the European Union, India, Japan, Russia, South Korea, and the U.S. It is designed to produce about 10 times the heating power fed into its plasma. Bogged by delays, a 2024 revision moved the start of research operations to 2034 and full deuterium-tritium operation to 2039, adding about €5 billion to the cost. IPR manages India’s home-grown tokamak reactors, including ADITYA and the Steady State Tokamak (SST-1). It is also the nodal domestic agency to manage India’s contributions to International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor.

The cost of a private tokamak depends on scale, Mr. Kaushal, who holds a Ph.D. from JNCASR, and a mechanical engineering degree from BITS Pilani, said. A compact research machine like PRAGYA is “a comparatively modest investment”, while one designed to reach net energy gain is far larger. Private fusion companies worldwide have raised over $13 billion, he said, and the leading net-gain programmes have each raised hundreds of millions of dollars or more.

Pranos Fusion says compact machines, HTS (high-temperature superconducting) magnets, and India’s manufacturing base can bring costs down substantially. It is backed by Ankur Capital, pi Ventures and Industrial47, and has raised $7.2 million. HTS electromagnets are wound from materials that carry electric current with no resistance when cooled below a critical temperature.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Pranos Fusion says compact machines, HTS (high-temperature superconducting) magnets, and India’s manufacturing base can bring costs down substantially. It is backed by Ankur Capital, pi Ventures and Industrial47, and has raised $7.2 million. articles.title: NASA telescope on verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission's chief scientist
An ageing NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower.
The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday (October 30, 2026).

Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission's chief scientist.

Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope's dwindling path.

Its cosmic cremation has the Swift team mourning, yet full of gratitude for the observations the telescope made during its 22 years in orbit. Swift blasted off on November 20, 2004, to search for some of the biggest explosions in the universe — gamma ray bursts and supernovas.

“We've known this day would come since before Swift was launched. At least in low-Earth orbit, what goes up must come down. And that end is catastrophic,” said Pennsylvania State University's John Nousek, an astronomer who led the control team.

Intense solar activity over the past few years dragged Swift down faster than usual. NASA hired Katalyst Space a year ago to mount a rush rescue. But the company's three-armed robot named Link ran into trouble after launching in July and got no closer than 7 miles to 9 miles (12 kilometres to 15 kilometres) to the telescope. Link plunged back to Earth in September.

Swift resumed observations once the rescue attempt was called off, discovering even more gamma ray bursts and other ultrahigh-energy events. But by late October, the telescope was too low to remain steady for observations, and its systems were shut down.

Its final tally — more than 2,000 gamma ray bursts and 1,400 exploding stars, not to mention a slew of comets, asteroids, and star-shredding black holes. The telescope's superpower was its ability to swivel swiftly — thus its name — toward erupting celestial events.

NASA considered Swift a first responder for the Hubble and Webb space telescopes and others that would follow its alerts and provide deeper investigations. Scientists are still figuring out how to fill the gap.

articles.title: ED arrests four more accused, including Myanmar national, in cross-border drug network
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chintuang was a Myanmar-based supplier of the 49.1 kg methamphetamine consignment seized in August 2025, while Lalrammuana was the main handler and Jabrul Haque its intended receiver at Damchhera-Kanhmun border; Abu Saleh was allegedly the operator whose account received ₹11.44 crore

The Enforcement Directorate has arrested four more accused, including a Myanmar citizen, in connection with an international cross-border “narco-hawala” network, following a recent multi-agency crackdown on the network. The agency has uncovered financial records purportedly showing that drug suppliers in Myanmar were also paid in kind.

As part of Operation Trident, simultaneous raids were earlier carried out at 38 locations across Assam, Mizoram, and Manipur, leading to the arrest of 18 accused persons and detection of ₹100 crore in “hawala” transactions on October 23.

In the latest arrests by the ED, the agency took into custody Myanmar national Thangcintuang alias Chintuang; Lalrammuana of Champhai district in Mizoram, Jabrul Haque from Sribhumi and Abu Saleh Md Saif Uddin from Karimganj in Assam. They were lodged in jail in connection with cases registered by the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB). The ED produced them before a local court and secured their 48-hour custody for interrogation.

According to the agency, Chintuang was the Myanmar-based supplier of the 49.1 kg methamphetamine consignment seized on August 21, 2025, while Lalrammuana was the main handler and Jabrul Haque its intended receiver at the Damchhera-Kanhmun border. Abu Saleh was allegedly the operator whose account received ₹11.44 crore, including ₹6.67 crore in cash, and fed the Champhai “hawala” accounts.

The ED allegedly seized cash books, registers and notebooks containing handwritten accounts of another accused Zenngaihniang’s “hawala” business during searches at her premises in Churachandpur town on October 23.

“The records reflect a regular currency-exchange and ‘hawala’ operation in which Indian currencies were received in cash and in bank accounts from persons in different parts of India, converted into Myanmari Kyat at daily rates of about 42 to 48 Kyat per Rupee, and paid out to persons in Myanmar,” it alleged.

The ED alleged that individual transactions ran up to ₹54.47 lakh a day, equivalent to about 26 crore Kyat, while cumulative transactions exceeded 43 crore Kyat. The agency found that ₹1.14 crore was paid to one handler within a week in April 2025. The records also allegedly showed transfers through Myanmar’s KPay app and the conversion of $10,816 at the rate of 4,150 Kyat per dollar between April 2025 and February 2026.

“Seven signed ₹10 notes, suspected to have been used as tokens for identifying the recipients of ‘hawala’ payments, and documents of an immovable property purchased for ₹60 lakh in the name of Zenngaihniang alias Taniang were also seized, and 991 bank accounts linked to the Churachandpur network were frozen,” said the agency.

The ED further alleged that the ledgers of Go Alpha Trip, a mini-ATM counter through which Taniang routed over ₹175 crore via the banking system, and statements in the connected Mizoram case revealed that drug money was also converted into ordinary goods to pay in kind.

The counter and the Mizoram mule accounts paid suppliers such as a flour mill in West Bengal, an edible oil trader in Assam, filling stations in Mizoram, grocery and medicine wholesalers, and footwear and cloth traders in Delhi, while the invoices were raised on third parties in Aizawl and border towns such as Champhai, Zorinpui, and Tlabung. The purchased goods were sent to Myanmar.

articles.title: Shetty Institute of Technology hosts TechNova and NextGen Hackathon in Kalaburagi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Shetty Institute of Technology (SIT), Kalaburagi, hosted TechNova 2026 and the AIC T-Hub NextGen Hackathon 2026 from October 27 to 30, bringing together 89 teams from educational institutions across the country.

TechNova, held on October 27 and 28, featured 26 teams from South India, with Robotics 2.0 among the major attractions. Winners in various categories received cash prizes ranging from ₹5,000 to ₹50,000.
The 36-hour NextGen Hackathon, organised in collaboration with AIC T-Hub on October 29 and 30, saw 63 teams comprising 220 students develop innovative solutions to real-world problems.
Pardha Saradhi of CMR College of Engineering and Technology, Hyderabad, won first place, followed by Smartronics of Symbiosis Skills and Professional University, Pune, and Latents of SIT, Kalaburagi.

Three teams – Technora Crews from SIT, Caffeine and Catastrophe from the Central University of Karnataka, Kalaburagi, and Core4 from NK Orchid College of Engineering, Solapur – were selected for further support from T-Hub.

SIT Director Anirudh Shetty said the events aimed to bring industry exposure, innovation opportunities and the start-up ecosystem closer to students in Kalaburagi. Director Shweta Shetty said such initiatives encouraged students to explore their potential, collaborate and develop practical skills beyond academics.
The four-day programme concluded with cultural performances, music, dance and other entertainment activities on October 30.

articles.title: Protesters smear ink on Addanda Cariappa’s face over his play on Gandhiji
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Controversial theatre personality and former Mysuru Rangayana director Addanda C. Cariappa was allegedly attacked and his face smeared with ink by a group of protesters during the staging of a play on Mahatma Gandhi’s assassination at Suchitra Film Academy in Banashankari on Saturday.

The incident occurred during the staging of Gandhi Hatheya Kicchu , organised by Rangabhoomi Trust (R), Kodagu, at Naga Links, Banashankari II Stage. Mr. Cariappa, who wrote and directed the play, was confronted by protesters who objected to its portrayal of Mahatma Gandhi.

The protesters, led by one Kushal Hanumegowda, lodged a complaint with the Banashankari police, accusing Mr. Cariappa of spreading misinformation about Gandhi and portraying him as “anti-national” and a “slave of Muslims” in the play. The complaint was signed by 14 persons.

The complaint further alleged that tickets for the Bengaluru staging had been sold on the black market in Mysuru. When the complainants questioned the alleged sale, Mr. Cariappa reportedly abused them using vulgar language.

The complainants sought legal action against Mr. Cariappa, the actors who performed in the play, and others associated with its staging.

articles.title: First import container arrives at Vizhinjam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The vessel carrying the first import consignment to Vizhinjam since full-scale export-import (EXIM) cargo operations commenced at Vizhinjam International Seaport in August called at the port here on Saturday, marking the beginning of a new chapter in the State’s maritime trade.

The first import container to Vizhinjam was booked from Ningbo in China and arrived aboard the vessel MSC Sabrina III. It was booked by BP2G Logistics and Ship Chandlers Private Limited, a Thiruvananthapuram-based start-up, on behalf of the city’s business enterprise, M/s Alteir Group.
The consignment comprises a full container load (FCL) of engineered building boards used in the construction sector as an alternative to conventional plywood.

With import operations now under way at Vizhinjam, containers can be unloaded, cleared and transported directly to markets across Keralam. This will reduce local entrepreneurs’ dependence on distant ports, helping them cut transportation costs and delivery times. The revenue generated through cargo handling and logistics activities will also remain within the State.

The development is expected to create employment opportunities for customs brokers, freight forwarders, transport operators, warehouse operators and port workers, while strengthening Keralam’s position as a maritime trade destination, authorities said.
