articles.title: Rahul Gandhi claims 2024 Lok Sabha elections ‘illegal’ over voter deletions | HIGHLIGHTS
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge lists six charges against Gyanesh Kumar, including facilitating vote theft, deleting 13.2 crore voter names and changing Form 6 without parliamentary oversight
BJP ridicules INDIA bloc’s mock Parliament, defends SIR, political double standards, and highlights alleged vote protection amid poverty claims.

Supporting the INDIA bloc’s ‘public impeachment’ programme, student activist Neha Bora accused CEC Gyanesh Kumar of misusing his office to benefit a political party and alleged that his appointment was undemocratic.

Congress leader Renuka Chowdhury dismissed the BJP’s denial of alleged voter deletions, accusing Prime Minister Narendra Modi of avoiding accountability in Parliament. She said the Prime Minister never appears in the House to answer questions.

Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal alleged that the Opposition had been denied a hearing in Parliament and other institutions for 12 years. He said Sunday’s rally at Ramlila Maidan would reflect public resentment against the government.

After the INDIA bloc’s symbolic ‘public impeachment’ programme against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Congress MP Shashi Tharoor said discussions had been dignified and positive. He expressed confidence that the same spirit would continue at Sunday’s rally, adding that large numbers of people were expected to attend.

In a post on X, Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi alleged that the deletion of one in every seven voters from electoral rolls amounted to an admission that the 2024 Lok Sabha election was illegitimate. He accused Gyanesh Kumar and others of treason and warned of action against them.
Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi claimed the Opposition had enough evidence against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to ensure his removal, warning the BJP against retaining him in office.

BJP MP Ravi Shankar Prasad criticised Rahul Gandhi for holding a symbolic ‘mock Parliament’ programme, accusing the Congress of ridiculing constitutional institutions. He also alleged that Jawaharlal Nehru became Prime Minister through vote theft and challenged Gandhi to resign.

Speaking at the INDIA bloc’s symbolic public impeachment programme against CEC Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi, TMC MP Mahua Moitra accused the Modi government and the Election Commission of undermining voting rights, claiming that 71% of deleted voters in West Bengal were Muslims and 51% were women.

Speaking at the INDIA bloc’s public impeachment programme against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi alleged that the deletion of 13.3 crore voter names had undermined the legitimacy of the 2024 Lok Sabha election. He claimed the number of deleted voters far exceeded the 3% vote margin between the Opposition and the BJP-led alliance.

articles.title: 43 women rescued in illegal human egg harvesting racket in Hyderabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police examine alleged recruitment of women across States, suspected use of rented premises and links with fertility centres and ART banks in Hyderabad

Eight people were arrested and 43 women from West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and other States were rescued during simultaneous raids at four premises in Hyderabad as police busted an alleged illegal human egg harvesting and commercial sale racket involving recruitment, transportation and accommodation of women for oocyte donation procedures.

The raids were conducted by Begumpet and Saroornagar police along with the Special Operations Team of the Malkajgiri Commissionerate at premises in Prakash Nagar, Begumpet, Erragadda, Saroornagar and Gopalapuram. Police seized documents, mobile phones and other material, while the identities, recruitment circumstances and medical histories of the rescued women are being verified.

Malkajgiri Police Commissioner B. Sumathi said the investigation was examining how women were recruited from different States and brought to Hyderabad after being offered ₹20,000 to ₹30,000 for each egg donation cycle. “We are examining the recruitment, transportation, accommodation and medical procedures, including whether the required legal and safety protocols were followed,” she said.

During the investigation, the women reportedly told police that hormonal injections and medicines were being administered to them in connection with the proposed procedures. Police seized five vials of Humog HP 150 I.U. injections, a syringe, two needles, Primolut and Meprate tablets and other material.

Police said inspections of the premises also raised concerns about the absence of authorised medical supervision and biomedical waste disposal arrangements. The investigation is also examining medical records, informed consent, donor frequency, insurance and safety protocols, as well as the statutory compliance of fertility centres and ART banks under the Assisted Reproductive Technology (Regulation) Act, 2021.

Among those arrested in connection with the Begumpet and Saroornagar cases are Amit Sharma, 44, described as the alleged main organiser, Nikkat Parveen, 31, an alleged co-organiser and recruiter, Reshma Khatoon, 26, an IVF agent or sub-agent, Meghavath Srinivas alias Sonu, 23, Jepray Pradeep, 27, Sk. Parveen, 42, Vijay Bhagwah Rao Salunke, 46, and Pankaj Soni, 52. Emirisheetty Durga Prasad, 42, a businessman from Saroornagar, was also arrested in connection with one of the Saroornagar cases.

Police said Amit Sharma had been operating from a rented premises at Prakash Nagar, Begumpet, for about two years, paying ₹50,000 a month. Nikkat Parveen allegedly recruited women, particularly from West Bengal, through agents and coordinated their transportation to Hyderabad.

The preliminary investigation indicates that organisers, recruiters, agents and intermediaries allegedly identified women in different States by offering monetary incentives, transported them to Hyderabad, accommodated them in rented premises and referred them to fertility-related service providers for ovarian stimulation and oocyte retrieval procedures.

The investigation is also focusing on identifying recruitment agents, tracing the transportation of the women, verifying suspected forged Aadhaar cards, affidavits and other documents, and tracing financial transactions and commissions. Police are examining whether there were instances of coercion, deception, exploitation or human trafficking and whether fertility centres and ART banks complied with statutory requirements.

The cases were registered under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Sections 29 and 33 of the Assisted Reproductive Technology (Regulation) Act, 2021. Further investigation is under way.

articles.title: IOC says crude Q2 price volatile as procurement swings between discounts and premiums
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Anuj Jain, Director (Finance) at Indian Oil also stated under-recoveries on LPG is projected at ₹309/cylinder in November and ₹370/cylinder in December.

Crude oil procurement remained volatile during the September quarter, with Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) sourcing supplies at discounts of up to $5 per barrel and premiums of as much as $12, Anuj Jain, Director (Finance), told investors during a post-results call on Saturday.

The Delhi-headquartered refiner’s net profit more than doubled year-on-year to ₹21,630 crore in the second quarter, supported by improved refining margins and a brief decline in benchmark crude oil prices.
Mr. Jain said LPG under-recoveries stood at ₹184 per cylinder in September before rising to ₹229 in October. These are projected to increase further to ₹309 in November and ₹370 in December.

Explaining the volatility in procurement costs, he said crude purchases during the quarter ranged from a discount of $5 per barrel to a premium of $12 against prevailing benchmark prices. In the first quarter, the range was from zero discount or premium to a premium of $18 per barrel.
Effective procurement prices depend on several factors, including whether supplies are contracted on a free-on-board (FOB) or delivered-at-place (DAP) basis, freight costs and the grade of crude.

Russian crude accounted for around 55% of IOC’s crude basket during the first half of the fiscal, followed by supplies from the Middle East, primarily Saudi Arabia and Dubai, at 24%. Africa, including Angola and Nigeria, contributed about 10%, while Brazil accounted for 7%. Supplies from the U.S. and Venezuela made up the remaining 2-5% and 3-4%, respectively.
Around 87% of the company’s crude procurement during the period came through spot sourcing. Mr. Jain said.
Responding to a question on whether spot purchases entailed higher costs, he said such sourcing did not necessarily mean paying a premium, as prices varied across region/geography.
“Now, within spot you have Russian crude. Sometimes, we are getting a high discount, sometimes we are paying a premium as well,” Mr. Jain said.

“In the few months, we have seen huge, discounted crude coming in from Iraq. So, the moment it is available, we are buying huge quantities from Iraq also. That used to be our staple diet before the [West Asia] crisis as well.”

articles.title: Clashes break out between police and protesters in Paris
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez warned of a “very high risk” of disorder, especially after dark on Halloween
The French government estimated that 320,000 people protested nationwide on Saturday (October 31, 2026) in demonstrations focused on high living costs, fewer than in previous demonstrations.

Mass protests on October 17 drew more than 500,000 people around France, and demonstrations on October 24 drew 410,000, according to government estimates. Organisers’ turnout estimates are much higher.

The Interior Ministry told reporters that of the 320,000 protesting on Saturday (October 31, 2026), 70,000 people are estimated to have turned out for the main protest in Paris, which police moved outside the city centre to reduce the risk of unrest around government buildings and tourist sites after a last-minute court battle.

This is the third consecutive weekend of protests over living costs and education, deploying 70,000 police and gendarmes and rerouting the Paris march to the capital's edge as youth-led demonstrations spread across Europe.
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez had warned of a “very high risk” of disorder, especially after dark on Halloween.

Paris police had banned union and “yellow vest” marches through the city centre, ordering demonstrations to follow a single route along the capital's outer boulevards, from Porte de Bagnolet to Porte de Charenton. Unions and student groups challenged the restrictions in court, but lost.
President Emmanuel Macron said on Monday (October 26, 2026) that marches would stay out of city centres to protect shops.
Police also barred entry to Place de la Republique and Les Halles, both hit by rioting and looting on October 17, from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. on Saturday (October 31, 2026) and Sunday (November 1, 2026).

Unaccompanied minors face a separate 9 p.m. curfew around the Champs-Elysees. A Paris court on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) suspended an earlier curfew on minors as a serious and illegal infringement of freedom of movement.
The movement began with high school students protesting school conditions and broadened into anger over living costs.

articles.title: Pakistan PM orders fast-tracking of development projects in Gilgit-Baltistan
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The development assumes significance for India as Gilgit-Baltistan is illegally and forcibly occupied by Pakistan
Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has directed officials to accelerate ongoing federal development projects in the controversial Gilgit-Baltistan region and ensure timely release of funds.

Mr. Sharif issued the directions while chairing a meeting in Islamabad on Friday (October 30, 2026) to review the progress of development projects in the region bordering China. Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Minister Amjad Hussain also attended the meeting.

The development assumes significance for India as Gilgit-Baltistan is illegally and forcibly occupied by Pakistan. The region is also a key component of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), which passes through Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.
India has consistently opposed the CPEC projects passing through territories under Pakistan's illegal occupation, citing concerns over its sovereignty and territorial integrity.

According to state-run broadcaster Radio Pakistan , Mr. Sharif directed the authorities to remove all bottlenecks hindering development projects on a priority basis and ensure effective coordination among the relevant institutions to expedite implementation.

The meeting also reviewed progress on hydropower, infrastructure and solar energy projects in Gilgit-Baltistan. The Prime Minister directed the earliest possible completion of the 100-megawatt solar power project initiated by the federal government for the region.
The meeting also discussed the completion of the China-funded Naltar power project and the installation of digital infrastructure in the region.
The Prime Minister called for regular monitoring of development projects, particularly those related to the energy sector.

A report of a committee constituted in July on the Prime Minister's directives was also presented at the meeting. It reviewed the status of ongoing federal development projects, hurdles in their implementation and measures needed to ensure their timely completion.
Mr. Sharif is likely to visit Gilgit-Baltistan on November 1, the state-run broadcaster reported.

The development assumes significance for India as Gilgit-Baltistan is illegally and forcibly occupied by Pakistan

Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has directed officials to accelerate ongoing federal development projects in the controversial Gilgit-Baltistan region and ensure timely release of funds.

Mr. Sharif issued the directions while chairing a meeting in Islamabad on Friday (October 30, 2026) to review the progress of development projects in the region bordering China. Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Minister Amjad Hussain also attended the meeting.

The development assumes significance for India as Gilgit-Baltistan is illegally and forcibly occupied by Pakistan. The region is also a key component of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), which passes through Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.

India has consistently opposed the CPEC projects passing through territories under Pakistan's illegal occupation, citing concerns over its sovereignty and territorial integrity.

According to state-run broadcaster Radio Pakistan , Mr. Sharif directed the authorities to remove all bottlenecks hindering development projects on a priority basis and ensure effective coordination among the relevant institutions to expedite implementation.

The meeting also reviewed progress on hydropower, infrastructure and solar energy projects in Gilgit-Baltistan. The Prime Minister directed the earliest possible completion of the 100-megawatt solar power project initiated by the federal government for the region.

The meeting also discussed the completion of the China-funded Naltar power project and the installation of digital infrastructure in the region.

The Prime Minister called for regular monitoring of development projects, particularly those related to the energy sector.

A report of a committee constituted in July on the Prime Minister's directives was also presented at the meeting. It reviewed the status of ongoing federal development projects, hurdles in their implementation and measures needed to ensure their timely completion.

Mr. Sharif is likely to visit Gilgit-Baltistan on November 1, the state-run broadcaster reported.

articles.title: Quad delivering results for people in Indo-Pacific: Rubio
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The group reviewed progress in turning shared priorities into real benefits for the Indo-Pacific region

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, Japan's Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi and Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong in Atlanta, U.S., on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting on Saturday (October 31, 2026).
The group reviewed progress in turning shared priorities into real benefits for the Indo-Pacific region amid plans to host a Quad leaders' summit in the Philippines next month.

“I was pleased to meet with my Quad counterparts in Atlanta and discuss the real progress we have made in turning our shared priorities into real benefits for the Indo-Pacific,” Mr. Rubio said in a post on X.

“As our nations continue building reliable and open supply chains, supporting next-generation technologies, increasing maritime cooperation, and securing critical minerals, the United States, Australia, India, and Japan are delivering results for our people and the nations in the region,” Mr. Rubio added.
Mr. Jaishankar said the meeting focused on giving impetus to bilateral relations.
“Appreciated @SecRubio’s hospitality in Atlanta for the @g20org FMM. Took stock of our bilateral cooperation,” Mr. Jaishankar said in a post on X.
This was the third Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting held this year. Earlier, the Ministers met in New Delhi in May and in Manila in July.
Moves are underway to convene a Quad Leaders' Summit, hosted by U.S. President Donald Trump on the sidelines of the ASEAN-East Asian Summits in mid-November.

articles.title: UN ends its Somalia political mission after three decades
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: UNSOM was established by the UN Security Council in 2013 to support Somali authorities in the transition to democracy and the rule of law after more than two decades of conflict involving militias, Islamist groups and criminal gangs

The United Nations political mission in Somalia ended on Saturday (October 30, 2026) after a two-year transition, closing a chapter of more than three decades of UN peacebuilding operations in the east African nation.

UNSOM was established by the UN Security Council in 2013 to support Somali authorities in the transition to democracy and the rule of law after more than two decades of conflict involving militias, Islamist groups and criminal gangs.
It started as UN Political Office for Somalia (UNPOS) in 1995.

In May 2024, Somalia's President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud asked the UN to end the mission ahead of the expiry of its mandate in October that year. He later revised the request, proposing a two-year transition period.
During the transition, UNSOM was renamed the UN Transitional Assistance Mission in Somalia (UNTMIS).

"Today is not an end to the partnership between the United Nations and Somalia-rather, it marks the conclusion of one chapter and the beginning of another," said Raisedon Zenenga, UNTMIS officer-in-charge and the UN secretary-general's deputy special representative for Somalia in a statement.
"While significant challenges remain, the closure of UNTMIS comes after considerable progress by Somalia since the early years of international efforts to support the country's recovery," he added.
The mission's mandates have been transferred to either Somali institutions or the UN country team.

The transition comes as Al-Qaeda-linked Al-Shabaab, which has fought the Somali government for two decades, continues to control large swathes of central Somalia despite a major international military campaign against it.

The fight against Al-Shabaab is increasingly threatened by international funding cuts, particularly after the United States withdrew all funding for a key UN logistics mission, casting doubt over the future of military operations.

articles.title: T.N. govt. raises DA for its employees from 60% to 63%
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A total of 16 lakh government employees, teachers, pensioners, and family pensioners will benefit from the increase
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Saturday announced a hike in dearness allowance (DA) for government employees and teachers with effect from July 2026.

A State government press release said the DA for employees had been increased from 60% to 63%, following a similar increase for Central government employees from July 2026. The revised DA would apply to the Tamil Nadu government employees and teachers with effect from the same date.

A total of 16 lakh government employees, teachers, pensioners, and family pensioners will benefit from the increase. The hike will cost the government ₹1,858 crore a year. “This will help them celebrate Deepavali happily,” the government release added.

articles.title: Take action against officials who arrested MIDS professor, Stalin urges T.N. government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: He says creating a society in which there is no room for questions is not a sign of good governance

DMK president M.K. Stalin on Saturday demanded action against police officials who had exceeded their remit by arresting Madras Institute of Development Studies (MIDS) professor Kalaiarasan. He also demanded action against the virtual miscreants whose activity had led to the arrest.

“Prof. Kalaiarasan was arrested over a comment on a fake ID. He raised his voice against the injustice meted out to him and came out. I appreciate him,” he said in a social media post. He added that creating a society in which there was no room for questions was not a sign of good governance. “Good governance is an administration that responds to the questions posed to it,” he said.
He said democracy demanded that a government accept criticism and rectify its mistakes. “Criticism should be countered with ideas, not the police,” he said.
In another message, Mr. Stalin condemned the escape of an autorickshaw driver, who had been arrested on charges of sexually assaulting a girl, from the Kolathur police station.

articles.title: ‘Administrative incompetence’ characterises TVK’s reign in the State, says Palaniswami
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Addressing a meeting in Maraimalai Nagar amid the 55th formation day celebrations of the AIADMK, the leader says even schemes launched by it, such as the marriage assistance scheme for women, were originally implemented during his party’s regime
AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami on Saturday criticised the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam-led government for its “administrative incompetence”.

Addressing a meeting in Maraimalai Nagar on the outskirts of Chennai amid the 55th formation day celebrations of his party, Mr. Palaniswami wondered what had been the achievement of the TVK-led government. Even schemes launched by it, such as the marriage assistance scheme for women, were originally implemented by the previous AIADMK regime, which had provided the financial assistance along with gold for thirumangalyam . In view of “steep hike” in the prices of construction materials, infrastructure work had come to a halt.

After coming to power, the TVK regime had stated publicly that the State power utility was facing a debt of ₹2.47 lakh crore. This being the case, how could it justify the move to procure power at costlier rates, the AIADMK leader wondered. “Rising” inflation, “growing” unemployment, “rampant availability” of drugs, “lack of security” for all sections of society, and law and order “deterioration” had marked the government’s reign. Though the ruling party claimed that it had been running a “clean government,” searches being conducted by the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti Corruption at several government offices led to the recovery of cash, giving the impression that bribery had been prevalent, Mr. Palaniswami argued.

Alluding to reports of dissatisfaction within the party and some legislators and functionaries of the AIADMK being wooed by other parties, the AIADMK leader said: “Some are trying to disturb the party; immobilise the party and split the party. They cannot even touch our workers.” He added that only in his party, the workers were being respected.

On the recent setback in the Madurantakam and Dharapuram byelections, Mr. Palaniswami attributed the victory of the ruling party to the latter’s alliance with a host of parties, whereas one of the allies of the AIADMK had stayed “neutral.” Besides, he referred to the allegation of the Communist Party of India (Marxist)’s leader P. Shanmugam regarding the distribution of money in the run-up to the by-polls.

He alleged that it was not C. Joseph Vijay who was the Chief Minister, but there were three persons who were functioning as Chief Ministers. While he did not name the three, he maintained that all the decisions concerning the administration were being taken by them.

Addressing a meeting in Maraimalai Nagar amid the 55th formation day celebrations of the AIADMK, the leader says even schemes launched by it, such as the marriage assistance scheme for women, were originally implemented during his party’s regime

AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami on Saturday criticised the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam-led government for its “administrative incompetence”.

Addressing a meeting in Maraimalai Nagar on the outskirts of Chennai amid the 55th formation day celebrations of his party, Mr. Palaniswami wondered what had been the achievement of the TVK-led government. Even schemes launched by it, such as the marriage assistance scheme for women, were originally implemented by the previous AIADMK regime, which had provided the financial assistance along with gold for thirumangalyam . In view of “steep hike” in the prices of construction materials, infrastructure work had come to a halt.

After coming to power, the TVK regime had stated publicly that the State power utility was facing a debt of ₹2.47 lakh crore. This being the case, how could it justify the move to procure power at costlier rates, the AIADMK leader wondered. “Rising” inflation, “growing” unemployment, “rampant availability” of drugs, “lack of security” for all sections of society, and law and order “deterioration” had marked the government’s reign. Though the ruling party claimed that it had been running a “clean government,” searches being conducted by the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti Corruption at several government offices led to the recovery of cash, giving the impression that bribery had been prevalent, Mr. Palaniswami argued.

Alluding to reports of dissatisfaction within the party and some legislators and functionaries of the AIADMK being wooed by other parties, the AIADMK leader said: “Some are trying to disturb the party; immobilise the party and split the party. They cannot even touch our workers.” He added that only in his party, the workers were being respected.

On the recent setback in the Madurantakam and Dharapuram byelections, Mr. Palaniswami attributed the victory of the ruling party to the latter’s alliance with a host of parties, whereas one of the allies of the AIADMK had stayed “neutral.” Besides, he referred to the allegation of the Communist Party of India (Marxist)’s leader P. Shanmugam regarding the distribution of money in the run-up to the by-polls.

He alleged that it was not C. Joseph Vijay who was the Chief Minister, but there were three persons who were functioning as Chief Ministers. While he did not name the three, he maintained that all the decisions concerning the administration were being taken by them.

articles.title: Higher Education Department wants HoDs to prepare students for placement; activists cry foul
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Tamil Nadu Higher Education Department has decided to task Heads of Departments (HoDs) of higher education institutions with the primary responsibility of preparing students for employment. Education activists, in response, have demanded a roll back stating that HoDs, who are subject experts, cannot be expected to perform the duties of placement officers.

The Department’s decision was communicated to the Commissioner of Collegiate Education, Director of Technical Education, and Registrars of all universities through a letter on Friday. The letter stated that the HoDs are required to tie up with about three to five private business houses relevant to their industry and formalise the association through signing of memoranda of understanding “to facilitate periodic interactions, feedback on curriculum, industry-related tasks and mini projects that familiarise students with industry practices”.

Basic sciences and Commerce departments, too will have to take part in the exercise, the letter read. The Department has prepared a list of 173 skills relevant to the subjects taught in Arts and Science colleges. For example, in Languages and Social Sciences such as History and Political Science, generic skills like digital marketing could be considered. The HoDs have been instructed to identify two-three verticals of skill training, each consisting of six skills.

The institutions have been instructed to approach Tamil Nadu State Council for Higher Education (TANSCHE) for training, support and other requirements. A list of five placement coordinators from each institution should be submitted to TANSCHE by November 16, the letter directed.

This directive has met with strong criticism from education activists who claim that the Tamil Nadu government was implementing various components of the National Education Policy 2020 one by one. The State Platform for Common School System – Tamil Nadu (SPCSS-TN), in a statement on Saturday, said that the NEP2020, in its background, stated that it aims to fulfil objectives from the 1986/1992 Education Policy that weren’t implemented. The 1986/1992 Education Policy had provisions to “commercialise education and transform higher education institutions into centres focussed solely on vocational training and employment”, it added.

“Can a professor or the head of a department in a college or a university perform the duties of a placement officer,” the statement, signed by P.B. Prince Gajendra Babu, general secretary, SPCSS-TN, asks. “It is the duty of professors and Heads of Department in colleges and universities to guide research, oversee academic processes—ranging from curriculum design to assessment—and manage the administrative tasks associated with these academic functions,” the statement read.

Through this order, the Department had delegated the responsibility of curriculum development to administrative officials, while tasking heads of departments in colleges and universities with duties that should rightfully be performed by placement officers, the statement added.

Putting forth similar arguments, S. Suresh, General Secretary, Tamil Nadu Government College Teachers Association, said that with over 7,000 vacancies in government Arts and Science colleges and several departments having no faculty members at all, the government should prioritise recruitment of permanent faculty.

articles.title: Ra’am and Joint List | The surge of the other
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Israel’s Arab parties made historic gains in elections but uncertainty remains whether the opposition bloc would join hands with them to form a government

On October 27, the day Israel went to the polls, the first election since the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack, the country recorded its highest voter turnout since 1999, at 77.7% But this was not the only story about the turnout.

Israel’s often overlooked Arab citizens, who make up some 20% of the population, made an overwhelming case for representation and change that day by turning out in massive numbers to vote. Exit polls recorded by Channel 12 estimated their turnout at nearly 80%, the highest in at least a decade.

For the far-right coalition led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu , the election was a “war for our home”, but for Arab parties, the political mobilisation meant meaningful representation in the Knesset , the Israeli parliament.

This mobilisation seems to have paid off. Arab parties have emerged as the third bloc after the elections. The Joint List and the United Arab List (Ra’am) have secured a combined 19 seats in the 120-member Parliament, their highest-ever tally.

Part of the credit goes to the Arab parties, which have actively mobilised their communities to vote. But much of it also goes to Mr. Netanyahu’s far-right government, whose policies and rhetoric, including the war on Gaza and escalating violence in the occupied West Bank, have heightened fears among Arab citizens.

While Arab citizens are affected like any other Israelis when it comes to national security, they’ve also borne the brunt of racism and violence. According to polls by the Israeli Democracy Institute, a party’s position related to crime in Arab society was one of the most important factors determining their vote.

Fear, as many experts have pointed out, has been their prime motivation, which Arab parties have been able to mobilise given the divisive campaigns launched by Mr. Netanyahu’s bloc. During the campaign, the Netanyahu camp put up billboards, saying it was ‘either the right or Palestine’. Even on the day of polling, the Prime Minister urged his supporters to go and vote, pointing to an Arab voter surge and calling it a matter of “life and death”.

While leaders of Arab parties have called Mr. Netanyahu’s attempts racist, they, too, have borne the brunt of discrimination. Like in the cases of previous elections, an attempt was made for disqualification of the Ra’am party and the Joint List (an alliance of Balad, Hadash and Ta’al) before the polls. The surge in voter turnout has helped them gain a significant number of seats, which would have made them kingmakers in a hung Parliament where no bloc has a clear majority. But neither side has expressed any willingness to form a government with Arab parties.

Mr. Netanyahu has accused the Arab parties of “stealing” the elections and has vowed to keep them out of power, while Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the opposition coalition, has been reluctant to join hands with them.

This reluctance is not new. The Ra’am party, led by Mansour Abbas, became the first Arab party in nearly 44 years to be part of a government in 2021 when they backed the Bennett-Yair Lapid government. Ra’am broke off from the Joint List. However, this experiment was short-lived as the coalition collapsed within a year. Ra’am returned to the opposition fold after Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition won the elections in 2022.

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Nearly every year since 1992, the United Nations General Assembly has passed a resolution calling on the U.S. to end its decades-old economic embargo on Cuba . As a result, the outcome at the UNGA resolution titled the ‘Necessity of ending the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the United States of America against Cuba’ passed on October 30, was expected. Surprisingly, the support for the resolution this year was dramatically lower than previous years. For the preceding decade, more than 180 countries of the 193-member UNGA had expressed their support for ending the embargo, but the numbers dropped to 165 in favour in 2025; this year’s tally dropped sharply lower, with 130 in favour, 25 abstaining and 17 countries voting against the resolution. The trend clearly points to efforts by the Trump administration to use its pressure on countries to change their votes, and many appear to have succumbed to those threats. Among those were several Latin American countries, that have more recently grown closer to the U.S., particularly after the operation in Venezuela in January 2026 , where U.S. marines abducted President Maduro and brought him to the U.S. for a trial. Countries in the region such as Costa Rica, Ecuador, Argentina, and Colombia that have downgraded ties with Havana, switched votes on the resolution. In addition, U.S. diplomats argued that Havana-Moscow ties emboldened Russia’s war in Ukraine , which led to several western countries switching their vote. Diplomats from Ukraine and Poland, for example, referred to Cuba’s ties with Russia while explaining their vote, and Germany and Italy switched for the first time in many years to abstaining on the resolution. While it is clear that the bulk of the Group of 77 and non-aligned states including India maintained their support on the resolution for Cuba, the vote by the others demonstrates a disquieting turn.

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s exasperation, during the Supreme Court’s hearing on October 29 on the “digital arrest” scams, that people still fall for such scams despite abundant warnings and orders from the Court is understandable. About ₹800 crore has been lost to these scams this year even after recoveries, a hefty sum from the savings of individual victims. But this is not merely about gullibility. Scammers posing as CBI or police officers succeed because their victims, older citizens in particular, defer to or fear law enforcement. When Indian police are widely seen as high-handed towards ordinary citizens and as serving only the powerful, the threat of an “arrest” over a video call cannot be that implausible for many. That said, the Court’s pressing of the Reserve Bank of India to finalise its KYC Amendment Directions, 2026, which require banks to flag suspected mule accounts and put temporary debit holds on them, is welcome. CBI investigations have shown that mule accounts are central to scammers laundering their proceeds after duping victims and that bank staff have, in some cases, helped open them. With the availability of complete transaction histories and AI tools, banks can now spot anomalous transactions faster. The Attorney-General’s assurance that the directions will be in force by December 31 is also welcome. The Court’s insistence that banks compensate victims addresses an issue with the RBI’s zero-liability provisions. Its 2017 circular covers only unauthorised transactions, leaving victims who were coerced into making transfers without any recourse.

By design, the Union Government controls both the Boards: they will be chaired by Union Minister for Labour Mansukh Mandaviya. They include seven members representing unorganised sector workers and seven members representing employers of the unorganised sector. 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Digital News Publishers Association’s (DNPA) challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 , and its Rules , has drawn attention to concerns that a law to safeguard informational privacy risks creating a serious chilling effect on the media. The absence of a specific exemption for journalistic activity could subject reporters investigating official misconduct or corruption to the obligations of a “data fiduciary”, requiring them to notify and seek consent from the very individuals they are investigating. Such onerous requirements could affect investigations undertaken in the public interest. The implications extend to routine newsgathering too, where personal information is integral to reporting. The omission is particularly consequential because the drafts in 2018, 2019 and 2021 carried a journalistic exemption. The Act already provides exemptions for certain forms of data processing, including for research and statistical purposes, making the denial of similar protection to journalists difficult to justify. Non-compliance can attract penalties of up to ₹250 crore, posing an existential threat to smaller and independent newsrooms. The DNPA petition also challenges Section 44(3), which amended the RTI Act, 2005, removing the earlier public-interest qualification concerning disclosure of personal information. The protection of personal information must not be absolute; an overriding public interest must remain a legitimate ground for disclosure, particularly when the information is held by public authorities. Investigations into corruption often rely on asset disclosures and tender documents containing personal data. Restricting access to these records risks reducing journalism to merely reproducing government releases.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: At Wednesday’s hearing of a petition on the Delhi SIR in the Supreme Court, Justice Joymalya Bagchi asked questions that cut to the heart of the Election Commission of India (ECI)’s SIR of electoral rolls . If an existing voter was “lax, inert or did not respond” to enumeration forms, was that a ground for the ECI to “forfeit his or her right to vote forever”? The Bench headed by the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said that the ECI was in “error” to force such voters, struck off for not returning enumeration forms, to reapply on Form 6 as if they were new voters. It asked why voters who had shifted residences could not just disclose details and why deleted voters could not fill enumeration forms belatedly. This is the central design flaw of the SIR as it shifts the burden of enrolment from the state to the elector, including those who have voted before, and treats a mere change of address as ground for deletion. The share of draft deletions recorded as “shifted” or “absent” rose from 55% in Bihar to 72% in States/Union Territories in Phase 3. In Karnataka, about 84 lakh electors were deleted, marked as “shifted” or “absent” during enumeration. But only a net of 8.2 lakh, including new electors, were added during the claims phase, with the final roll being 64.5 lakh short of the projected adult population. Requiring moved voters to re-register as fresh applicants defeats the ECI’s historic mandate of widening the franchise, which was inherent in the 2002-03 intensive revision, where enumerators enrolled shifted voters at their new homes and the Chief Electoral Officer reconciled the old entries.
